candidates.title: Albertans to vote on opting out of federal programs — while keeping cash
candidates.description: When referendum day arrives in Alberta on Oct. 19, the focus won’t just be on separation and immigration. One of four constitutional questions will ask voters if they support a push to amend the Constitution so Alberta can opt out of federal programs, while keeping the cash.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: With millions of dead oysters and mounting debt, P.E.I. farmers fear they'll lose everything
candidates.description: Disease has blighted P.E.I.’s oyster industry, wiping out entire crops. Oyster farmers say they need more help to survive the crisis and are worried their independent farms may be snapped up by bigger corporations with deeper pockets.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: World's tallest totem pole comes down in Alert Bay, B.C., after more than 50 years
candidates.description: The world’s tallest totem pole was brought down this week in Alert Bay, B.C., a community off the coast of northeast Vancouver Island. For two 'Na̱mǥis chiefs, the pole — recognized in the Guinness Book of World Records — represented much more than its height.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Is Christine Fréchette exploiting the trade war, or just doing her job as Quebec premier?
candidates.description: The leader of the Coalition Avenir Québec has come under fire from her political opponents after interrupting her election campaign and convening her cabinet amid the ongoing trade war with the United States. Is Christine Fréchette using the moment for political gain, or just doing her job?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Canadian renaissance': Stars share their love for homegrown films on the red carpet at TIFF
candidates.description: As tensions between Canada and the U.S. creep into the film industry, Jay Baruchel is more than confident his country can stand toe to toe with its southern neighbour. He's one of a number of Canadian actors sharing their love of the country's film industry and Canada in general on the TIFF red carpet after the festival kicked off Thursday night.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nova Scotia’s RSV vaccine program leaves out vulnerable adults, patients say
candidates.description: Nova Scotia has an RSV vaccination program that provides free vaccines to three groups of people, but it leaves some seniors and immunocompromised people out. Paying out of pocket for the vaccine costs a few hundred dollars.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New statues added to controversial Prime Minister's Path in Wilmot, Ont.
candidates.description: Four statues of former Canadian leaders were added to the Prime Minister's Path project in Wilmot, Ont., on Saturday. Not everyone was pleased.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Provinces are turning to U.S. health-care workers to help with shortages. And it’s working
candidates.description: With shortages of nurses, physicians and other health workers, some provinces are actively recruiting U.S. health-care professionals — and they’re getting results.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta separatists expect a win, regardless of numbers that say otherwise, poll suggests
candidates.description: A political scientist and pollster say that mismatch of expectations has consequences for what comes next and Albertans shouldn’t expect this issue to be put to rest with this one vote.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian women improve to 3-0 at wheelchair basketball worlds in Ottawa with win over China
candidates.description: Canada's women's wheelchair basketball team improved to 3-0 in the preliminary round at the world championships in Ottawa with a 66-62 win over China on Saturday at TD Place.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bears, caribou and other animals are messing with this researcher's equipment, and he's got photos to prove it
candidates.description: Lucas Brehaut was hoping there’d be a lot of interest in his research, though it might be a case of “be careful what you wish for.” Caribou, moose, black bears, wolves, rabbits and owls have been messing with his research equipment.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Time for a digital divorce? Trade war puts spotlight on Canada's relationship with U.S. big tech
candidates.description: Tensions between Canada and the United States have raised concerns about Canada's digital sovereignty, but what does that term mean, and how can Canada promote it? Experts say it's about making sure Canada has tech alternatives and can effectively regulate all things digital, but that can prove difficult.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Canada is everyone, for everyone': Carney meets with Alberta remain campaigners
candidates.description: The head of the Forever Canadian group campaigning for Alberta to remain in the federation said Friday Prime Minister Mark Carney has been a "calm" and "reassuring" presence for Albertans.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Elk involved in nearly two-thirds of aggressive encounters in national parks, study finds
candidates.description: Researchers analyzed Parks Canada data collected from 2010 to 2023 on aggressive wildlife encounters and what people were doing when they occurred. The researchers found that quiet activities like hiking, walking and sightseeing were when many encounters occurred.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Poutine pit stops and political optics: Why food matters on Quebec's campaign trail
candidates.description: A plate of poutine has become a familiar sight on the Quebec campaign trail. Political analyst Antonine Yaccarini says these stops are carefully planned to make politicians appear accessible and connected to voters — but the strategy can backfire if it feels staged.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gander gave Americans a lift on 9/11. 25 years later, it was the other way around
candidates.description: On a day when the compassion of people in Gander, N.L. was being celebrated, a chance encounter at a chicken restaurant led to a tour bus of Americans repaying the favour.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Biologists are fighting this invasive plant – by hand – to protect some Quebec waters
candidates.description: Water chestnut, an invasive aquatic species, multiplies quickly and blocks the light other species rely on. The watershed council for the Vaudreuil-Soulanges area is working to eradicate it from the Ottawa River and the Lake of Two Mountains.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Drone-powered ad for PC Health chatbot slammed as 'dystopian' by some residents
candidates.description: On Thursday night, more than a thousand drones lit up the sky above Toronto's waterfront displaying a list of health-related questions in what turned out to be an ad campaign for a new President's Choice AI-powered chatbot.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Will the U.S. midterm results affect Trump's tariffs on Canada? Democrats think yes
candidates.description: Although Canada and the United States remain entrenched in their trade war positions, some Democratic politicians say a strong showing for their party in the upcoming U.S. midterm elections in November will make a difference in the fight.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Search underway for about 130 people after Indonesian ferry overturns
candidates.description: A ferry overturned in bad weather in Indonesia's Java Sea on Sunday, leaving about 130 passengers and crew missing, rescuers said. At least 107 people were rescued and the bodies of six passengers were recovered.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Prince Harry and Meghan's U.K. return gets a very British roast in Saturday Night Live UK sketch
candidates.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s highly publicized return to England got the full Saturday Night Live UK treatment — and in true British fashion, the welcome was served with a distinctly chilly reception.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Céline Dion ends 6-year concert hiatus with emotional Paris performance
candidates.description: Thousands of devoted fans flocked to the Paris suburb of Nanterre on Saturday as Celine Dion returned to the stage for her first full concert in six years, opening a sellout Paris residency after a battle with a rare neurological disorder sidelined her career.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Turkish authorities launch crackdown on 2SLGBTQ+ and HIV support groups
candidates.description: Turkish authorities cracked down on multiple 2SLGBTQ+ groups and individuals early Sunday morning, detaining dozens of members, breaking into association offices and raiding popular hangouts.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 1 dead after Iranian commercial ship struck near Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media say
candidates.description: State-run IRNA news agency quoted the Qeshm governor as blaming a "terrorist enemy." He also said the person killed was among the cargo vessel's 10-member crew, and that authorities had not yet identified the projectile.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lithuania says drone sighting turns out to be flock of birds, after NATO summons jets
candidates.description: Lithuania said that a perceived drone sighting in its airspace earlier on Sunday that prompted authorities to close Vilnius airport and NATO to summon at least one fighter jet turned out to be a flock of birds.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strike kills 2 people in Gaza, medics say
candidates.description: An Israeli airstrike on Sunday killed at least two Palestinians in a vehicle and wounded 13 others in the Gaza Strip, medical staff said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Your guide to the U.S. midterms, and why they're crucial for Donald Trump
candidates.description: Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming U.S. midterm elections and why they're potentially crucial to how U.S. President Donald Trump wields power in his final two years in the White House.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iraq scrambles to address fallout from alleged militia attack on Saudi oil pipeline
candidates.description: Iraq’s government was racing Saturday to contain the fallout after local Iran-backed militias were accused of attacking and shuttering a key Saudi pipeline.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump's call for united Ireland draws swift rejection from pro-British unionists
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he would "love" to see British-run Northern Ireland unify with Ireland, remarks made during a visit to Dublin that drew a sharp response from pro-British unionists in Northern Ireland.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Deadly Russian strikes hit Ukraine after Putin's warning to European leaders
candidates.description: Russian strikes killed three civilians and wounded dozens in Ukraine, local officials said Saturday, after Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that sending European troops into Ukraine would amount to direct conflict with Russia.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Spain's soccer federation will fund egg freezing. Is this a win for female athletes?
candidates.description: While fertility preservation measures like egg freezing are typically presented as another way to give women in elite sport greater freedom to decide if and when to become mothers, some experts and advocates say they're concerned that it could send the message that athletes should delay motherhood.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 15-year-old rescued after clinging to capsized boat for days in Alaska's Bering Sea
candidates.description: Bobbing for days atop a capsized skiff in Alaska's frigid Bering Sea, a 15-year-old boy held on until he was rescued by a fishing vessel this week, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The price of diesel is skyrocketing. Here's why Canadians may soon feel it at the grocery store
candidates.description: With diesel prices skyrocketing due to ongoing global conflicts, filling up the trucks that carry food and goods across Canada has never been more expensive, experts say — and Canadians could be feeling it soon.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI-driven 'worms' that learn on the fly are the latest potential threat to your devices, researchers say
candidates.description: Artificial intelligence researchers are warning the public to use strong passwords and promptly install software updates on their devices to combat "AI-driven computer worms," a new breed of cyber-threat they say can launch custom attacks on devices, sapping processing power and information as they hunt for new victims.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trade 'war' or not, are Canada and the United States now dug in?
candidates.description: Jamieson Greer, the U.S. Trade Representative, might not like to think of it as a trade 'war.' But whatever you call it — a difference of opinion? an incongruity? the unpleasantness? — it's been going for more than 19 months. And it seems now that it could be several more months before hostilities are reduced, let alone ceased.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stellantis signs MOU with Canadian armoured vehicle maker on potential sale of Brampton, Ont., plant
candidates.description: Automaker Stellantis says it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel on a potential sale of its idled Brampton, Ont., assembly plant.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
candidates.description: The former UK PM said "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Six dead, 130 missing after Indonesian ferry capsizes in Java Sea
candidates.description: Ships and helicopters are searching for those missing from the Virgo Transport 8 ship, which had encountered bad weather.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Turkish police detain dozens in raids on gay bars and homes of LGBTQ+ activists
candidates.description: Human rights groups in Turkey have accused the government of using a family- values campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Iran war reshapes Brics ties but also exposes divisions
candidates.description: Brics members agree they need a new global order but it's harder to answer what should replace it and how to get there.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump doubles down on united Ireland comments on day two of visit
candidates.description: The US president was speaking at the Irish Open on Sunday and said "many people agree" with his comments.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Legendary Canadian boxer George Chuvalo dies aged 89
candidates.description: The heavyweight champion took on the likes of Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier, and was known for never once getting knocked out or knocked down.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US congressman swims to safety after his plane is forced to land on a lake
candidates.description: The small plane carrying Rep Tom Tiffany had a mechanical issue that forced the pilot to make an emergency landing on a Wisconsin lake.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: They lost their jobs after posting about Charlie Kirk, but some have no regrets
candidates.description: Some people fired in the wake of Kirk's assassination have won big settlements from employers, others have had to start over from scratch.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Afghan woman deported from US in first use of 'alien terrorist' court
candidates.description: The legal US resident was never charged with a crime, but was deported due to her family links to terrorism.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Only Roland Garros towel left, says Ukraine tennis player after Russian strike hits flat
candidates.description: Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russians seek answers over hundreds missing after Ukraine's 2024 incursion
candidates.description: Officials say more than 300 Russians remain missing after the 2024 Kursk offensive, but no-one really knows the true figure.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Dramatic insider warnings over AI fall flat with some in Silicon Valley
candidates.description: A recent spate of stark warnings about the dangers of AI has been met with scepticism by executives and investors.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Best friends for decades - until a DNA test revealed they were sisters
candidates.description: Meena Geltink and Minal Tijssen were adopted from orphanages in Mumbai in the 1980s and grew up in the Netherlands.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Critics celebrate Céline Dion's 'high-stakes' comeback show in Paris
candidates.description: The iconic Canadian singer kicked off her long-awaited comeback show in Paris on Saturday, after a six-year hiatus due to health issues.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump's comments on a united Ireland may have targeted audience across the Atlantic
candidates.description: Nobody could have predicted that today's main global headline would be Trump's desire to see a unified Ireland.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
candidates.description: It comes as the AI firm's boss has called for the technology's development to be slowed down, citing "serious" risks.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Five night sky events to look out for this autumn
candidates.description: From meteor showers to a November supermoon, there are a number of impressive sights to behold in the autumn night sky.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Residents and officials meet on dredging concerns
candidates.description: Officers plan to meet with a complainant in the coming days over the dredging at St Aubin's Bay.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs
candidates.description: Sarah Hickey and her team help keep nearly 20,000 acres of upland in the Isle of Man healthy.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Indonesian passenger ship overturns, sparking search for at least 129 missing
candidates.description: Indonesian rescuers said about 130 passengers and crew are missing after a ferry carrying more than 240 people sank in bad weather in the Java Sea on Sunday.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV
candidates.description: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'BRICS' forum brings together emerging economies, aimed at countering western dominance
candidates.description: India hosts the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi this weekend. BRICS is a grouping of major emerging markets and developing countries.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Saudi Arabia forced to shut down crucial Red Sea pipeline after attacks
candidates.description: The Iran-backed Houthi militia captured a strategic Red Sea port city this week. NPR's Scott Simon talks to April Longley Alley of the Washington Institute.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The secret quest to preserve Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh's diaries
candidates.description: Leading Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh has documented Israel's occupation of the West Bank since day one. Fearing the occupation might consume his archive, he secretly moved it to Scotland
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: BRICS leaders meet in India as wars and US tensions test the bloc
candidates.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosts Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders of the BRICS nations for a summit on trade, investment, and global conflicts.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Yemen's Houthis capture a Red Sea island in threat to shipping
candidates.description: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have captured a strategic island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The move threatens Saudi oil exports through a key commercial lane. And Saudi Arabia said it shut down a major oil pipeline as a precaution after it came under attack.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
candidates.description: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Amid war and sanctions, many Iranians are losing their jobs and struggling to get by
candidates.description: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new tax incentive could lead to more films being made in the U.S. rather than abroad
candidates.description: President Trump and Congress are weighing in on potential federal tax incentives for film production. It's hoped the tax credit would keep production of films and TV in the U.S. rather than overseas.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Anthropic and OpenAI CEOs call for AI development to slow down, OpenAI to delay IPO
candidates.description: Dario Amodei and Sam Altman are the latest to urge caution amid fears the industry is racing too fast to build powerful AI while safety measures lag.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Actor Tatyana Ali is advocating for Black and Indigenous maternal health
candidates.description: Actor Tatyana Ali says her healing journey after a traumatic childbirth has inspired her advocacy for Black maternal health, including support for midwives, doulas and other birth workers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Black women are more likely to experience pregnancy trauma and have their pain ignored
candidates.description: Black mothers in the U.S. are three times as likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. Actress Tatyana Ali became an advocate after her own awful experience giving birth.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A cancer survivor hoped to work — then she lost her Medicaid disability coverage
candidates.description: As state governments grapple with how to determine who's sick enough to be excused from new Medicaid work requirements, some families are already struggling with what illnesses guarantee health coverage because of a disability.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: * WHAT...West winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph possible. * WHERE...Snowy and Judith Mountains, Fergus County below 4500ft, and Judith Basin County and Judith Gap. * WHEN...From Monday morning through Monday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

candidates.description: At 135 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near Mashulaville, or 9 miles west of Macon, moving southeast at 10 mph. candidates.description: At 1135 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated that heavy rain has moved east of the Havasupai Creek drainage north of Supai, though additional storms are possible through the afternoon. Beaver Falls, Mooney Falls and Little Navajo Falls. This includes the Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158. This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds... Second Chance Camp Site. This includes the following swimming holes... All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai. This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers... Sinyella Canyon, Colorado River, Little Coyote Canyon and Havasu Creek.

candidates.title: M 6.5 - 126 km NNE of Teluknaga, Indonesia
candidates.description: The United States Geological Survey reported an earthquake of magnitude 6.5. The event occurred near 126 km NNE of Teluknaga, Indonesia. Official monitoring data may be updated as scientists review additional measurements.
candidates.author: U.S. Geological Survey
